errors: No outright error. One gap: operations 2 (erasing markings) and 6 (capping holes) can leave the stable/anabelian range. For example, capping a boundary of a (0,3) piece gives an annulus. So they must be restricted to cases preserving 2g−2+ν>0, and the page does not state this.

The 'amalgamation without erasure' (5) and erasure of circles (7) are listed separately. Ordinary gluing of surfaces is their composite, and the twist ambiguity arises precisely in 7, which is only implicit here.

missed.claim: In 1983 Grothendieck explicitly enumerates the generating operations on decorated stable surfaces and on their combinatorial types (weighted graphs), as a structured system of functors with twist isomorphisms. This is essentially the axiomatics of a modular operad in groupoids, with sum as monoidal structure, cutting as edge insertion, erasing circles as contraction, and forgetful maps. It predates Getzler–Kapranov (1998). The resemblance is noted informally in the GT/operad literature (Lochak, Schneps, Horel, Boavida–Horel–Robertson), but this precise catalogue is not documented there.
missed.quote: Catalogue opérations + structures ... 4) découpage (partiel) 5) amalgamation ou recollage (sans gommage !) 6) bouchage de trous (= gommage des cercles de raccord) 7) gommage des cercles internes ... foncteurs et iso "twist"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence of Grothendieck's operadic-style formalization of the Teichmüller tower, relevant to modern work identifying GT with automorphisms of (genus-0 or higher-genus) modular operads.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an outline, not a result. Its catalogue of operations with paired inverses and the type-functor diamond is an early, fairly explicit operadic axiomatization of the tower. However, the general idea is visible in the Esquisse and was later systematized independently, so it would interest historians more than surprise specialists.
